definitions.explanation: Behavior or words that are disrespectful or lacking in courtesy.
An interjection used when excusing oneself, typically by older men. Somewhat old-fashioned.

examples.japanese: {失敬|しっけい}な{態度|たいど}だ。
{失敬|しっけい}なことを{言|い}うな。
それは{失敬|しっけい}。{言|い}い{過|す}ぎた。
examples.english: Pardon me. I went too far.

examples.japanese: では、これで{失敬|しっけい}するよ。
examples.english: Well then, I'll be taking my leave.

examples.japanese: ちょっと{失敬|しっけい}。{先|さき}に{一本|いっぽん}もらうよ。
examples.english: Excuse me. I'll take one first.

examples.japanese: おや、{失敬|しっけい}{失敬|しっけい}。{名前|なまえ}を{間違|まちが}えてしまった。
examples.english: Oh, pardon me, pardon me. I got the name wrong.

notes: Functions as a na-adjective ({失敬|しっけい}な), a suru-verb ({失敬|しっけい}する — to excuse oneself, or colloquially to swipe/pilfer something), and an interjection. As an interjection, it has a somewhat old-fashioned, masculine feel and is associated with middle-aged or older men. {失礼|しつれい} is the more common modern equivalent for excusing oneself. The suru-verb form can also colloquially mean to help oneself to something without permission.
